description: Rick's long relationship with Australia runs from an earlier journey through Sydney, native ingredients and Tasmania to a 2026 return across New South Wales, where coastal seafood, farming, migration and regional producers define the food of the country he regards as a second home.

s15e00.description: From Mollymook and Sydney to Tasmania, Rick searches for ingredients changing Australian cooking, revisiting Sydney Fish Market, learning about native foods around Botany Bay and examining Tasmania's wallaby, whisky and sustainable salmon.

s15e01.description: Rick returns to Sydney, revisiting the city where his Australian attachment began and meeting old friends and new cooks while tracing the immigrant and local influences that reshaped the food he remembers.

s15e02.description: North of Sydney, Rick explores the Central Coast through chefs, foragers and producers, looking at how beaches, bushland and an outdoor way of life dictate what people gather, grow and cook.

s15e03.description: Rick retraces the north-coast road he hitchhiked as a teenager, meeting cooks and communities whose relaxed dining culture is inseparable from the subtropical coast and its produce.

s15e04.description: The journey turns inland to Moree and Bourke, where farming communities confront distance, heat and difficult conditions with a practical food culture built on resilience and regional history.

s15e05.description: In the Riverina, Rick meets farmers and producers who transformed both landscape and livelihood to create one of Australia's major food bowls, finding innovation behind an apparently traditional agricultural region.

s15e06.description: Rick finishes on the Sapphire Coast, one of his favourite stretches of Australia, where cold clean water, exceptional seafood and familiar faces turn the final journey into a return to the country he treats as a second home.
